name: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd.

profile.description: Brookfield Asset Management is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, investing across infrastructure, renewable power and transition, private equity, real estate, and credit (including Oaktree, whose remaining stake BAM bought in July 2026). In Q2 2026, fee-bearing capital reached $672B (+19% YoY), fee-related earnings rose 20% to $808M, and fundraising set a quarterly record of $77B [1]. Connor Teskey became CEO in February 2026, succeeding Bruce Flatt, who remains Chair and CEO of parent Brookfield Corporation [3].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Over five years Brookfield launched multiple new flagship franchises. These include the Global Transition Fund strategy, a $40B insurance/wealth investment mandate from Brookfield Wealth Solutions (the Just Group mandate), and full ownership of Oaktree (completed July 2026). It also reorganized in 2022 into a separately listed, capital-light manager [1][4]. AI Deployment (2/2): BAM is shipping AI investment products to clients. Its AI infrastructure strategy reached $5B of commitments at first close, and it has a strategic partnership with OpenAI and a $25B Bloom Energy financing program [1]. Market Share (2/2): $672B of fee-bearing capital and $163B of trailing-12-month fundraising place BAM among the global leaders in alternatives, and it is widely regarded as the largest private infrastructure and renewables investor [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Named projects include a $100B AI data-center campus plan at the DOE's Paducah, Kentucky site (July 2026) and a €30B French government AI framework [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Not applicable to an asset manager; no R&D is disclosed.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Brookfield's purpose of investing in and operating the 'backbone of the global economy' (infrastructure, power, essential real assets) for long-term owners is specific and different from peers that compete on financial engineering. It has guided capital allocation toward transition and AI infrastructure [1][3]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific BAM foundation or dollar figures for community programs were found. ESG discussion centers on disputed net-zero accounting and Westinghouse's tritium supply chain [4]. Employee Retention (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong. Teskey was prepared over a four-year succession process, Flatt called it 'no real transition', and the firm is described as rewarding executives with long-term equity [3]. No firm-wide turnover data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying was found. The company repurchased $200M of its own shares in Q2 2026 [1].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically as a Growth stock. The 4.16% yield exceeds 2%, but BAM Ltd has paid dividends only since its December 2022 spin-off (under 5 years), so it fails the Dividend sleeve's 5-year history test [5]. D/E of 34.5%, ROE of 26.8% (2x), profit margin of 48.9%, and PEG of 0.86 (2x) all score 1.00. YoY revenue growth of 60.8% scores 1.00; it is inflated by the Oaktree consolidation. The 2-year revenue CAGR derived from reported revenue ($3.71B in 2023 to $4.61B in 2025, 11.4%) scores 1.00 at 2x weight; a 5-year figure is not meaningful because of the 2022 restructuring [5]. Forward P/E of 22.4 scores 0.939. Weighted sum 9.94/10 rounds to 10. Daily dollar volume of about $135M clears the liquidity floor. Note that the reported payout ratio is 108%, but this metric is not scored for Growth-sleeve stocks [5].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): BAM earns management fees on long-dated, locked-up private capital invested in physical assets such as power plants, data centers, pipelines, and real estate. AI cannot replace those assets or the relationships needed to raise and deploy institutional capital at the $77B-per-quarter scale [1]. AI increases demand for BAM's core product: management says trends such as artificial intelligence and digitization are driving demand for investment capital [3]. Some exposure remains in office real estate and in AI-driven automation of parts of the credit and wealth businesses, which keeps the score below the top band. AI Opportunity (1/1): The AI infrastructure strategy has $5B of commitments, alongside the OpenAI partnership and the Bloom Energy and French government AI frameworks, all of which generate fee-bearing capital [1].

infinite_game.summary: Brookfield is built for duration. It holds long-life real assets, manages permanent and long-dated capital, and has a decades-long culture of owner-operators that produced a four-year CEO succession [1][3]. Sinek would admire the patience and continuity, and the repeated reinvention from Brascan-era conglomerate to global alternatives manager. He would be wary of the asset-gathering language ('best year ever', record fundraising) and the disputed net-zero claims, which suggest growth targets sometimes run ahead of the cause [1][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The idea of building and operating the essential infrastructure of the global economy (power, transition, digital, and now AI compute) connects BAM's work to a future beyond fees. It shows up in capital allocation such as the transition funds and the Paducah AI campus [1]. It falls short of 3 because outside messaging still leans heavily on fundraising totals and fee growth ('we expect our best year ever') [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): Brookfield's partnership culture shows in its leadership continuity. The CEO transition to Teskey was planned over four years, Flatt called it 'no real transition', and the firm is described as collaborative and disciplined and as rewarding executives with long-term equity rather than carried interest [3]. Senior executives tend to spend decades at Brookfield, which suggests a durable circle of safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that credits Blackstone, KKR, or Apollo as benchmarks. BAM's public messaging emphasizes record fundraising and scale advantages rather than learning from rivals [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Brookfield has reinvented itself more than once. It went from a Canadian conglomerate to a global real-asset owner, then separated in 2022 into a capital-light, separately listed asset manager. It is now building an insurance/wealth and AI-infrastructure platform and has taken full control of Oaktree [1][4]. Each shift kept the long-term real-asset ownership core.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Committing tens of billions to AI infrastructure and energy transition before demand is proven, including a $100B Paducah campus plan and a €30B French framework, shows willingness to make long-term bets [1]. However, the 2021 net-zero claim had to be walked back after criticism of its 'avoided emissions' accounting. That suggests positioning sometimes outruns principled follow-through [4].

investment_thesis: BAM is a high-quality fee compounder. Q2 2026 fee-related earnings rose 20% to $808M ($3.2B over the trailing twelve months, +19%), distributable EPS rose 15% to $0.44, fee-bearing capital grew 19% to $672B, and quarterly fundraising set a record $77B [1]. The Oaktree buy-in, the $40B Just Group mandate, and Angel Oak add about $200M of run-rate fee-related earnings [2]. The $5B AI infrastructure first close, the OpenAI partnership, and the $100B Paducah AI campus put BAM at the center of AI-era capital formation [1]. Metrics are excellent: ROE 26.8%, profit margin 48.9%, D/E 34.5%, PEG 0.86, and a 4.16% dividend yield [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation, payout, and cyclicality in fundraising. At 22.4x forward and 27.7x trailing earnings, BAM is priced for continued high-teens fee growth, and Q3 fundraising is expected to fall well short of Q2's record $77B because $40B of that came from a single related-party mandate (Just Group, via Brookfield Wealth Solutions) [2][5]. The reported payout ratio of 108% leaves little room if fee growth slows. Related-party flows from Brookfield Corporation and Brookfield Wealth Solutions make headline growth hard to judge [1][5]. Reputational and ESG risks include the disputed net-zero claim and Westinghouse's tritium supply role, which has placed Brookfield on some European exclusion lists [4]. A CEO transition (February 2026) and a large AI-infrastructure concentration add execution risk if AI capex slows [1][3].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November): fee-related earnings growth sustained near the 20% Q2 pace and confirmation of management's 'best year ever' outlook [1][2]
Additional closes of the AI infrastructure strategy beyond the $5B first close, and progress on the $100B Paducah, Kentucky AI data-center campus [1]
Full-year contribution from the Oaktree buy-in and the Just Group / Angel Oak mandates, adding about $200M of run-rate fee-related earnings [2]
key_risks: Fundraising normalization after the record $77B Q2 (of which $40B was a single related-party mandate), slowing fee-bearing capital growth from 19% [1][2]
A dividend payout ratio of about 108% of reported earnings, which constrains dividend growth if fee-related earnings disappoint [5]
Concentration in AI data-center and power investments that would be hurt if hyperscaler AI capex slows, plus ESG exclusion risk from Westinghouse's nuclear supply chain [1][4]
